content: These products should not be used during treatment with the suppository form of this medication and for three days after completing the treatment. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used if absolutely necessary. Discuss the potential risks and benefits with your doctor. Pregnant women should exercise caution when using the vaginal applicator. Follow your doctor’s instructions carefully regarding the proper insertion of the medication using the applicator. The manufacturer advises against using this product during the first three months of pregnancy. It is not known whether this medication passes into breast milk. Drug interactions can alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all products you use, including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. If this medication is swallowed, it may be harmful. In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. To help prevent vaginal yeast infections, thoroughly dry the genital area after showering, bathing, or swimming. Avoid wearing tight jeans, nylon underwear, pantyhose, wet bathing suits, or damp/sweaty exercise clothes for extended periods. This medication has been prescribed specifically for your current condition and should not be used for other purposes. If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store the cream or suppository at room temperature. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. This medication is used to treat vaginal yeast infections. Terconazole reduces vaginal burning, itching, and discharge associated with this condition. It is classified as an azole antifungal. If you experience fever, chills, flu-like symptoms, stomach or abdominal pain, or foul-smelling vaginal discharge, do not use this medication. Read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist before starting this medication and each time you get a refill. This product is for vaginal use only. Wash your hands before and after use. Avoid contact with your eyes. If the medication gets into your eyes, rinse them immediately with plenty of water. Use this product as directed by your doctor, typically once daily at bedtime for three or seven days, depending on the product. Follow all preparation and usage instructions provided in the product package. If using the cream, use the applicator. If using the suppository, you may use either the applicator or your finger to insert it. Unwrap the suppository before use. Follow the package instructions for filling the applicator with cream or inserting the suppository. Lie on your back with your knees bent toward your chest. Insert the applicator or suppository into the vagina as far as it will comfortably go. Slowly press the plunger of the applicator to release the medication. Clean the applicator with warm, soapy water, rinse well, and dry. Continue using this medication every day until the full prescribed amount is finished, even if symptoms disappear after one to two days. You may use this product during your menstrual period. Do not use tampons or douches while using this medication. Inform your doctor if your condition does not improve or if it returns within two months. Possible side effects include headache, increased vaginal or urethral burning, itching, pain, or menstrual cramps. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefit to you outweighs the risk of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before using this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other azole antifungal agents (such as clotrimazole or fluconazole), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. Ask your doctor whether you can engage in sexual intercourse while using this product. The suppository form (but not the cream form) may damage rubber products such as latex condoms, diaphragms, or cervical caps, potentially leading to failure and resulting in pregnancy. Do not use these products during treatment with the suppository form and for three days after completing the treatment.
